from rich.style import Style

def test_hash_after_clear_meta_and_links():
    # Create a style with meta and link
    style = Style(color="red", meta={"key": "value"}, link="https://example.com")
    original_hash = hash(style)
    
    # Clear meta and links
    cleared_style = style.clear_meta_and_links()
    cleared_hash = hash(cleared_style)
    
    print(f"Original hash: {original_hash}")
    print(f"Cleared hash: {cleared_hash}")
    
    assert original_hash != cleared_hash, "Hash should change after clearing meta and links"

        print("Test passed!")
    except AssertionError as e:
        print(f"Test failed: {e}")

        print(f"An error occurred: {e}")

from rich.text import Text
from rich.highlighter import ReprHighlighter

def test_url_tilde():
    text = Text("https://example.com/~user")
    highlighted = ReprHighlighter().highlight(text)
    # The style for URLs in ReprHighlighter is "repr.url"
    # We check if the tilde is part of the URL span
    for span in highlighted.spans:
        if span.style == "repr.url":
            print(f"Found URL span: {span}")
            assert "https://example.com/~user" in highlighted.plain_text
            # Check if the span covers the whole URL including the tilde
            # The span is (start, end, style)
            url_text = highlighted.plain_text[span.start:span.end]
            print(f"URL text: {url_text}")
            assert url_text == "https://example.com/~user"
            return
    
    print("No URL span found!")
    assert False

if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        test_url_tilde()
        print("Test passed!")
    except AssertionError as e:
        print("Test failed!")
        raise e

from rich.ansi import _ansi_tokenize, _AnsiToken

def test_private_escape_sequences():
    # \x1b0 and \x1b? are private escape sequences
    text = "\x1b0test\x1b?"
    tokens = list(_ansi_tokenize(text))
    print(f"Tokens: {tokens}")
    # Expected: only the plain text "test" should remain if the escape sequences are stripped
    # Currently, they are likely treated as plain text.
    assert tokens == [_AnsiToken(plain="test")]

        print("Test passed!")

from fastapi.security.utils import get_authorization_scheme_param

def test_get_authorization_scheme_param():
    # Test case 1: Single space (correct)
    assert get_authorization_scheme_param("Bearer xxx") == ("Bearer", "xxx")
    
    # Test case 2: Multiple spaces
    assert get_authorization_scheme_param("Bearer   xxx") == ("Bearer", "xxx")
    
    # Test case 3: Trailing whitespace
    assert get_authorization_scheme_param("Bearer xxx ") == ("Bearer", "xxx")
    
    # Test case 4: Both multiple and trailing
    assert get_authorization_scheme_param("Bearer   xxx  ") == ("Bearer", "xxx")
    
    # Test case 5: No header
    assert get_authorization_scheme_param(None) == ("", "")
    assert get_authorization_scheme_param("") == ("", "")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        test_get_authorization_scheme_param()
        print("All tests passed!")
    except AssertionError as e:
        print(f"Test failed: {e}")
        exit(1)

from rich.prompt import Prompt

def test_case_sensitive():
    # This is a bit tricky because Prompt.ask reads from stdin.
    # We can mock stdin or just test the check_choice method directly.
    prompt = Prompt(choices=["Paul", "Jessica", "Duncan"])
    assert prompt.check_choice("Paul") is True
    assert prompt.check_choice("paul") is False
    print("Current behavior: case-sensitive check works as expected (case-insensitive fails).")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_case_sensitive()

from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
import io
from contextlib import redirect_stdout

def s_start():
    print("SYNC START", flush=True)

def test_startup():
    # We use a new FastAPI app for each test to ensure startup events are triggered
    app = FastAPI(on_startup=[s_start])

    @app.get("/health")
    async def health():
        return {"ok": True}

    f = io.StringIO()
    with redirect_stdout(f):
        with TestClient(app) as client:
            client.get("/health")
    
    output = f.getvalue()
    print(f"Output: {output}")
    if "SYNC START" in output:
        print("SUCCESS: Startup event was called")
    else:
        print("FAILURE: Startup event was NOT called")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_startup()

from rich.highlighter import ReprHighlighter
from rich.text import Text

def test_url_highlighting():
    highlighter = ReprHighlighter()
    
    # Case 1: URL without @ (should work)
    text1 = Text("http://example.org")
    highlighter.highlight(text1)
    print(f"Text 1: {text1.plain}, Spans: {text1.spans}")
    
    # Case 2: URL with @ (should be fully highlighted)
    text2 = Text("http://user@example.org")
    highlighter.highlight(text2)
    print(f"Text 2: {text2.plain}, Spans: {text2.spans}")

    # Case 3: URL with @ and path/query
    text3 = Text("http://user:pass@example.org/path?query=1")
    highlighter.highlight(text3)
    print(f"Text 3: {text3.plain}, Spans: {text3.spans}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_url_highlighting()

app = FastAPI()

@app.post("/test")
async def test_endpoint(value: Optional[str] = Form(None)):

client = TestClient(app)

def test_empty_string_as_none():
    # When sending an empty string for an optional field with None default,
